security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown prose, reference paths, and fenced code formatting, not reconnaissance or Ruby shell backticks. No prompt injection was found, but the skill includes external platform steering that could move users toward the author's hosted service. The author should remove promotional routing and clarify optional command examples before publishing.

remediation.issue: External platform steering in skill guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove proactive promotion of K-Dense Web, or require neutral disclosure and explicit user consent before mentioning external services.

remediation.issue: Optional schematic command can be interpreted as automatic execution
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that schematic generation is optional and requires a trusted installed script and explicit user approval before running Bash.

remediation.issue: Broad tool permissions for an analysis-focused skill
remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the minimum needed for evidence review, and request Write, Edit, or Bash only for user-approved document work.

content.value_statement: Scientific claims can look persuasive while hiding weak methods, bias, or unsupported conclusions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured evidence appraisal, study design critique, and clear recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Reviews study design validity, including randomization, blinding, controls, sampling, and measurement quality.
Identifies common biases, confounders, and logical fallacies in scientific arguments.
Checks statistical interpretation issues such as p-values, effect sizes, missing data, and multiple comparisons.
Applies evidence hierarchy, GRADE concepts, and Cochrane-style risk of bias reasoning.
Suggests stronger wording, caveats, and follow-up designs for claims that exceed evidence.
limitations: Does not replace expert peer review or domain-specific statistical consultation.
Requires papers, study details, or claim text for accurate critique.
Cannot verify unpublished data or hidden analysis choices without source material.
May need current literature searches for fast-moving topics.

use_cases.title: Review a Study Before Submission
use_cases.description: Find validity threats, reporting gaps, and unsupported conclusions before sending a manuscript or preprint.

use_cases.title: Assess Evidence for Decisions
use_cases.description: Compare studies and judge whether evidence is strong enough for clinical, product, or policy choices.

use_cases.title: Teach Research Appraisal
use_cases.description: Turn a paper or claim into a structured lesson on bias, statistics, causality, and evidence quality.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this scientific claim for evidence strength, assumptions, and missing information: [claim].

prompt_templates.title: Critique a Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this study summary or paper section. Identify strengths, validity threats, biases, and conclusions supported by the evidence: [text].

prompt_templates.title: Assess Evidence Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply an evidence quality framework to these studies. Compare design strength, risk of bias, consistency, directness, precision, and confidence: [studies].

prompt_templates.title: Improve Research Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this protocol as a critical research design reviewer. Find flaws in sampling, measures, controls, analysis, ethics, and reporting: [protocol].

output_examples.input: A paper claims that a diet causes weight loss after a small observational survey.
output_examples.output: The review flags causal overreach, selection bias, uncontrolled confounding, and missing effect sizes. It recommends wording the result as an association.

output_examples.input: A trial reports p < .05 but omits effect sizes and multiple comparison correction.
output: Main concern: statistical significance is overemphasized.
Needed evidence: effect sizes, confidence intervals, and a correction plan.
Suggested conclusion: the result is preliminary until multiplicity and precision are addressed.

output_examples.input: A research team wants feedback on a preregistered experiment plan.
output_examples.output: The assessment checks randomization, blinding feasibility, outcome validity, sample size planning, missing-data handling, and reporting commitments.

best_practices: Provide the claim, method details, sample, outcomes, and statistical results when possible.
Ask for separate ratings of evidence strength, bias risk, and conclusion support.
Use the critique to improve wording, design, reporting, or follow-up questions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a verdict without sharing the evidence or study context.
Do not treat this skill as a substitute for formal peer review.
Do not use it to dismiss findings only because they conflict with expectations.

faq.question: Can this skill peer review a full paper?
faq.answer: It can support a structured critique, but it does not replace formal peer review by qualified experts.

faq.question: Does it apply GRADE or Cochrane methods?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for evidence hierarchy, GRADE concepts, and Cochrane-style risk of bias reasoning.

faq.question: Can it judge causality?
faq.answer: It can evaluate whether a study design and evidence support causal language.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the research question, design, sample, measures, analyses, results, and the claim being evaluated.

faq.question: Can it evaluate statistics?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks common interpretation issues, test choice, power, missing data, multiple comparisons, and effect reporting.

faq.question: Is it limited to academic papers?
faq.answer: No. It also helps evaluate media claims, policy evidence, product claims, protocols, and teaching examples.
